title: Broccoli, fresh, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli is an edible flower head of Brassica oleracea var. italica, a relative of cabbage, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts. Fresh broccoli is usually steamed, boiled or roasted without added fat, preserving most of its nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli contains more vitamin C than an orange.
In ancient Rome broccoli was called “little tree”.
There are over 100 varieties, including green, purple and Roman broccoli.
Broccoli is rich in glucosinolates, compounds that may support the body’s detoxification processes.
In Japan broccoli is often served as a salad with soy sauce and sesame seeds.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: One hundred grams of broccoli provides about 90 mg of vitamin C, which supports immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety and supports gut microbiota.

items.title: Rich in phytochemicals
items.content: Sulforaphane and other glucosinolates have antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Broccoli has only about 35 kcal per 100 g, making it an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Gas formation
items.content: Broccoli contains raffinose, which can cause gas in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with medication
items.content: Large amounts of vitamin K may affect the efficacy of anticoagulants such as warfarin.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergic reaction to cruciferous vegetables.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Broccoli can be eaten raw in salads, steamed, boiled for 3–5 minutes, or roasted with herbs. When cooking without added fat, a steamer or microwave is recommended.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh broccoli in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, loosely packed in a perforated bag. Use within 3–5 days. For freezing, blanch for 2–3 minutes, cool quickly and pack in airtight bags.
